title: Derived functions of profinite parameters for a constant continuous model
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$ on all profinite sets, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work with internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. All sites, parameter sets and resolutions lie in compatible coefficient universes.

Let $X$ be an affine $k$-scheme and $P$ a profinite set. Let $\rho_P:X[P]\to X$ be the inverse limit of the finite disjoint-union projections indexed by finite quotients of $P$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Fix a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space $M$. Put $M_F(Q)=C(Q,F\otimes_E M)$, where $F\otimes_E M$ has its finite-dimensional product norm topology. Let $C_F[P]$ be the free internal $C_F$-module on the condensed set $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$; free means left adjoint to forgetting to condensed sets. Let $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}$ be the right derived internal module Hom in its second variable. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\delta_{X,P,M_F}:R(\rho_P)_*(p_{X[P]}^*M_F[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}p_X^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F).$$
It is normalized by the free-module/tensor/internal-Hom adjunction and evaluation of functions: its degree-zero comparison is the exponential-law map, sending a section on a relative $P$-test object to the corresponding $P$-indexed function. It is natural in $M$, in continuous maps of profinite parameters, under pro-etale base change of $X$, and under $C_{F,X}$-linear maps between the supplied constant models. For such a map varying over a profinite $Q$, naturality is an equality over $X[Q]$, allowing simultaneous continuous maps $Q\times P'\to P$ of parameters, rather than pointwise equality on $Q$. For the inclusion $E\to\Omega$, the comparisons commute after scalar restriction with $M_E\to M_\Omega$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. All continuous functions are retained. No completion or finite-subextension-valued replacement is used.

proof.text: Write $\Lambda=C_F$, $A=\Lambda[P]$, $N=M_F[0]$ and $B=p_X^*\Lambda$. Work interchangeably with internal modules and their section-ring module sheaves: the exact equivalence preserves underlying sheaves, tensor and its derived model, and takes the right-adjoint internal Hom to K-injective derived sheaf Hom with the same evaluation. It likewise transports the entire direct-image functor and its derived adjunction. On the condensed-point site the same exact monoidal equivalence identifies internal and sectionwise modules; preservation of K-flat and K-injective resolutions follows by transporting their defining Hom/tensor acyclicity tests. Thus no change of coefficient category or completion is involved.

source.place: 08J7 and 08J9; internal/sectionwise transport by the cited exact monoidal equivalences.

proof.text: There is a canonical identification $p_X^{-1}h_P=h_{X[P]}$. Indeed, on a geometrically w-contractible affine test $V$ both sides are $C(\pi_0V,P)$, with the same restrictions; geometric w-contractibility implies the site evaluation criterion needed by the two cited evaluation statements. Such affines cover every affine test by the single-cover theorem; arbitrary tests have affine open covers. Consequently the identifications determine an equality of sheaves. Pullback also takes $A$ to $B[h_{X[P]}]$: for any $B$-module $T$, the pullback adjunction and the free-module adjunction identify maps from either object to $T$ with maps $h_P\to p_{X*}(\operatorname{Forget}T)$, since module direct image has that underlying sheaf. Yoneda gives the isomorphism, normalized on generators. Similarly $\rho_P^*p_X^*N=p_{X[P]}^*N$ by composition of the condensed-point pullbacks.

source.place: Example 3.1; component evaluation and the free-module universal property.

proof.text: The small pro-etale site of $X[P]$ is the slice $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/X[P]$; use only clause (1) of the localization node. Put $U=X[P]$ and take a K-injective resolution $p_X^*N\to J$. The free-generator adjunction, applied on each slice over $V$, identifies $\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_U],J)(V)$ with $J(V\times_XU)$, degree by degree and with the same differential. By preservation of K-injectives under localization, $J|_U$ is K-injective and resolves $p_{X[P]}^*N$. Thus the identical complex $\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_U],J)=\rho_{P*}(J|_U)$ computes both $R\mathcal Hom_B(p_X^*A,p_X^*N)$ and $R(\rho_P)_*p_{X[P]}^*N$. This is the canonical derived identification, natural in the object, the parameter maps and further localization because its degreewise maps evaluate the same free generator.

Pull back the evaluation $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A,N)\otimes_\Lambda^{\mathbf L}A\to N$ along $p_X$, using its exact inverse image and canonical derived tensor comparison. Transposition defines
$\beta_X:p_X^*R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A,N)\to R\mathcal Hom_B(p_X^*A,p_X^*N)$.
This defines a morphism before any assertion that it is invertible. Under restriction to a slice it is the same evaluation-adjoint morphism: the cited slice evaluation/transposition identities identify the two transposes. In particular its restriction to a test $W$ is $\beta_W$, using the cartesian coefficient identification for $p_W$.

source.place: 08J7 tensor-Hom adjunction; derived monoidal pullback and evaluation normalization as in the cited nodes.

proof.text:
Let $W\to X$ be a geometrically w-contractible affine test and put $S=\pi_0W$. The component morphism gives $p_W^*=\pi_W^*q_S^*$. Restriction $q_S^*$ from the profinite site to its slice over $S$ commutes with derived internal Hom for arbitrary unbounded complexes. The component theorem then identifies
$\pi_W^*q_S^*R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(A,N)$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{p_W^*\Lambda}(p_W^*A,p_W^*N)$.
Both arrows are normalized by evaluation, so their composite is precisely the restriction of $\beta_X$ constructed in step 4. Hence $\beta_X|_W$ is invertible. Every affine test has such a cover by the single-cover theorem. The cone therefore has all cohomology sheaves zero locally and hence globally; $\beta_X$ is invertible. Compose its inverse with step 3 to obtain $\delta_{X,P,M_F}$ in the direction stated in the item.

source.place: Proposition 4.3(1); restriction of derived internal Hom is Stacks 08JB.

proof.text: The slice identification evaluates a free generator, and $\beta_X$ is the transpose of pulled-back evaluation. Thus the inverse composite has exactly the specified degree-zero exponential-law normalization, sending a section on $V[P]$ to its corresponding $P$-indexed function. Uniqueness of transposes gives naturality in $N$ and in maps $h_{P'}\to h_P$, hence in $M$ and continuous maps $P'\to P$. The same argument on a slice, with the slice evaluation identities, gives pro-etale base change. If a base-changed scheme is not affine, this equality holds on its affine open cover and glues. These are equalities of the derived morphisms, since they are obtained by transposing identical evaluation morphisms.

source.place: 08J7 and 08JB; uniqueness of tensor-Hom transposes and slice compatibility.

proof.text: Choose bases only to check the remaining linear-map clause. The supplied constant models are $B^r$ and $B^s$, since continuous functions into a finite product are products of continuous functions. On every slice an arbitrary map between them is a matrix of sections of $B$; all comparison maps above are $B$-linear and respect finite sums. They therefore commute with this matrix, including matrices not pulled back from the condensed point. This description is independent of the checking bases. Over $X[Q]$, repeat the construction in that slice. A continuous $\alpha:Q\times P'\to P$ induces a map of parameter objects over $X[Q]$. Transposing the two proposed composites gives the same evaluation morphism there: for a local family $f$, it sends $(q,p')$ to $u(q)(f(q,\alpha(q,p')))$. This notation describes evaluation on the entire parameter object, not evaluation only at its points. The equality follows from the free-generator adjunction and associativity of composition, so it holds over $X[Q]$, including all higher derived terms by the same transposition identity.

source.place: 08J7 and 08JB; formal linearity and evaluation on the slice, with finite free models.

proof.text: Finally apply the coefficient map $C_E\to C_\Omega$ and the module map $M_E\to\operatorname{Res}M_\Omega$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The free-generator coefficient-extension identification sends the generator $[a]$ to $[a]$. The canonical coefficient-comparison arrows for internal Hom and direct image are mates of these evaluation/module maps. After scalar restriction both composites in the requested square transpose to the identical map, evaluating a function and then applying $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Hence their mates agree. This argument uses the derived extension/restriction adjunction (K-flat tensor for extension) and does not assert that scalar extension is exact or that the scalar-comparison arrows themselves are isomorphisms. All operations used the original sheaves $C(Q,F)$ and $C(Q,F\otimes_E M)$; no finite-subextension-valued or completed model has entered.

source.place: 08J7: compatibility of evaluation with coefficient maps, by uniqueness of adjunction mates; derived coefficient extension is ringed pullback for the identity topos.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 4.3(1), combined with Stacks slice localization and derived tensor-Hom. The parameter identification and coherence argument are written here, not asserted to be a theorem quoted verbatim in the blueprint.

On side-live the item is unsplit and its statement is identical. Neither the item nor any cited node is in route-pivot-dropped. There is no re-split note, no SGA citation, and no DAG cycle. The item is true. Its target is Rρ_*ρ^*N' = RHom_B(B[h_{X[P]}],N'), with p_X^{-1}h_P = h_{X[P]}. This leaves the claim that p_X^* commutes with RHom(Λ[P],N), and it can be checked on w-contractible W by p_W = q_S π_W: the slice restriction q_S^* commutes with RHom, and π_W^* does by HRS 4.3(1). I re-derived that clause from (4.2) plus full faithfulness of π_U^* for arbitrary unbounded K, L. The RΓ clause is full faithfulness applied to (Λ_S, K). Step checks: step 2 combines basis evaluation with the components-maps bijection, both natural in V, and covers affine X by det-pe-hypercover-single-cover (quasi-compact). Step 3 is an elementary slice calculation using K-injective restriction (08FI) and is correctly marked. Step 4 constructs β before claiming invertibility. Step 5 uses exact restriction of RHom plus the new node, then concludes globally because cohomology sheaves vanishing on a cover vanish. Step 6 checks the H^0 exponential law. Step 7 checks matrix linearity because M_F = C_F^r, and the X[Q]-family version. Step 8: the mate under derived extension/restriction from projection-mate-exact; free modules are flat; no exactness of scalar extension is claimed. Edge cases P empty, P a point, M = 0 and non-complete Ω all pass. The new node lem-sfb-wcontractible-component-derived-hom is exactly HRS 4.3(1) plus its RΓ corollary.
